_description: Material technique: Panning UV / Scrolling textures. Fundamental for flowing effects — fire, water, energy, magic, clouds, force fields.
overview: Panning UV shifts texture coordinates over time, creating the illusion of movement without particle simulation. Combined with multiple layers at different speeds, it creates complex flowing visuals cheaply.

steps.note: PanSpeed is Vector2 (U direction, V direction). Positive U = scroll right, positive V = scroll up.

steps.nodes: Result → UV input of Texture Sample
steps.note: Texture must have Wrap addressing mode (not Clamp)

dual_layer_panning.description: Two textures panning at different speeds/directions for complex motion

steps.action: Layer A: noise texture at speed (0.1, 0.2)
steps.nodes: TexCoord * ScaleA + Time * SpeedA → Sample TextureA

steps.action: Layer B: same or different noise at speed (-0.05, 0.15)
steps.nodes: TexCoord * ScaleB + Time * SpeedB → Sample TextureB
Multiply, Add, or Lerp depending on desired look

options.multiply: Creates interference pattern, good for caustics/water
options.lerp_with_mask: One layer visible through gaps in other

dual_layer_panning.note: Different directions + different speeds = organic, non-repeating look

distorted_panning.description: Use one panning texture to distort the UVs of another

steps.nodes: TexCoord + Time * DistortSpeed → Sample DistortionTex → RG channels

steps.action: Use distortion to offset main texture UVs
Sample main texture with distorted UVs

distorted_panning.note: This is the KEY technique for realistic fire, lava, and energy. The distortion creates organic wavering.

fire_material.layers: fire gradient (vertical pan up) + noise distortion (slow pan)
fire_material.note: Vertical panning + horizontal distortion = flickering flames

water_surface.layers: normal map A + normal map B at different scales and angles
water_surface.note: Two normal maps panning creates convincing water ripples

energy_shield.layers: hex pattern + noise, both panning slowly
energy_shield.note: Combined with fresnel for edge glow

lava_flow.layers: lava color texture + heavy noise distortion
lava_flow.note: Slow speed + heavy distortion = thick viscous flow

magic_trail.note: Pan direction opposite to ribbon travel direction

cloud_layer.note: Extremely slow speeds for environmental clouds

speed_guidelines.very_fast: 0.5-2.0 — speed lines, laser beams, dash trails
speed_guidelines.note: These are multiplied by Time node which runs in seconds

common_mistakes: Texture set to Clamp instead of Wrap → texture stops at edges instead of repeating
Both layers same speed and direction → no complexity, looks like single sliding texture
Pan speed too fast → looks mechanical and CG, most natural motion is slower than you think
Not using distortion → clean panning looks artificial, always add some UV distortion
Forgetting to subtract 0.5 from distortion texture → UV offset is biased, texture shifts off-center
